## 2026-06-16 UI/UX reconfiguration quick wins shipped

Six SPA-only UI/UX PRs merged to prod and verified by the operator. A dropped whole-app reconfiguration spec (`KitStak-UIUX-Reconfiguration-Plan-2026-06-16.md`) was verified against the code first and found to be roughly seventy percent already built: the state-driven detail action bars (Send, Approve, Receive payment, all gated by `canTransition`), the customer hub related-record sections, the dashboard work-card queue, the Cmd or Ctrl-K command palette, and the empty-state coaching all already existed. So the spec's P2 (spine collapsed by default), P3 (detail pages are read-only, only Download PDF), and P5 (hubs have no spokes) were refuted by the code, and Pattern D (an interactive lifecycle rail) was excluded because it reverses the locked UX-Q7 display-only decision. The verified delta shipped as six small presentation-layer PRs: no schema, no migration, no RLS, money, idempotency, audit_log, or contract change. CHANGELOG `0.20.0`. Closeout journal `03-workspace/journal/2026-06-16-uiux-reconfiguration-closeout.md`.

Merged to prod, all six squash-merged to `main` and the prod deploy is green (`deploy-prod` success, CI and CodeQL green). #300 (`01a4d60`) resolves detail-subtitle names so the customer or source no longer flashes a raw UUID on first paint (the existing `fallbackLabel` helper). #301 (`e432ed1`) trims the dashboard marketing hero to a compact operational header, keeping the work-card queue. #302 (`e775b7a`) default-opens the SPINE backbone only, adds a type-to-filter box, and role-scopes the Admin links, plus deriving the persisted-expanded allow-list from `SIDEBAR_MODES` (closing a latent `wms` omission). #303 (`ed0393d`) adds a visible topbar Search button over the existing command palette and an entitlement-scoped Create menu. #304 (`f76dbd4`) adds a hand-rolled accessible URL-synced `Tabs` primitive. #306 (`d19bb14`) converts the customer hub to tabs.

One bundle catch worth recording. Wiring `useCapabilities` into the eager Topbar folded the capability matrix into the index chunk and pushed it to 41.9 kB gz, over the 40 kB `size-limit` budget. Fixed by lazy-splitting the Create menu into its own `CreateMenu.tsx` chunk (the same discipline that keeps the Sidebar lazy); the index landed back at 38.65 kB gz. Index headroom is now tight (about 1.4 kB), not the larger margin assumed earlier; PROJECT.md's 29.95 kB figure was stale.

A stacked-PR note for next time. #305 (the customer hub tabs, stacked on the #304 Tabs primitive branch) was auto-closed by GitHub when #304 was squash-merged and its branch was deleted, because the child's base branch vanished. The single-file change was cherry-picked onto fresh `main` (which now carries the Tabs primitive) and re-opened as #306, which merged clean. Lesson: merge stacked PRs bottom-up and hold off deleting the parent branch until the child is in, or merge the child first.

## 2026-06-15 WMS add-on shipped (Body B, B0 to B4) plus FSM RPC grant hardening

The sixth add-on is live on prod. WMS (warehouse execution) deepens the spine's warehouse-level stock to bin level without replacing it: a nullable `location_id` rides the existing append-only `stock_movements` ledger, the sum of the bins equals the warehouse `quantity_on_hand` by construction, and turning `plugins.wms` off leaves the spine totals untouched. Gated `plugins.wms` (default off) at the `/wms` root behind the new `wms-api` edge bundle. Migrations 0105 to 0111 (prod at max 0111). CHANGELOG `0.18.0`. ADR `docs/adr/0002-spine-plus-addons-and-wms-sixth-addon.md`.

Phases. B0 chassis (#267, migration 0105 seeds `plugins.wms`, extends `seed_org_settings`). B1 warehouse locations (#268, 0106: bins, shelves, racks, docks, staging areas; a config table with an `active` boolean, not a registered state machine). B2 the stock-movement bin dimension (#269, 0107: the additive nullable `location_id` plus forward refs `lot_id` and `license_plate_id`, the `bin_stock_levels` rollup, `recompute_bin_stock_level`, and one AFTER INSERT trigger firing both rollups; sum-reconcile holds by construction, closing the carried operator stop-point risk R-W12-CO-02). Receiving-to-dock (#271, 0108: a single header `dock_location_id` on `receiving_orders`, one dock per receipt, applied by the receipt emitter to every line). B3 directed putaway (#272, 0109 `putaway_tasks`, FSM suggested / in_progress / done / cancelled; completing emits `transfer_out` at the source dock and `transfer_in` at the destination bin, a warehouse-flat internal move that invents no new ledger type). B4 lots (#273, 0110: the `lots` parent and end-to-end lot capture reconciling at the (location, lot) grain; FEFO is groundwork only via the `expiration_date` index).

Hardening. Migration 0111 (#274) revokes `EXECUTE` from `authenticated` on the 18 state-changing action and transition RPCs. The SPA never calls any RPC directly (zero `.rpc()` in `apps/web/src`); every action RPC runs from an Edge Function through the service-role `admin()` client, so the `authenticated` grant was an unused attack surface. `service_role` retains `EXECUTE`, so the Edge path is unchanged; the RLS-context helpers and the recompute / seed / audit helpers keep their grant. Closes `F-Wave12-WMS-FSM-RPC-GRANT-HARDEN-01`.

There is no WMS closeout journal yet (the journals stop at A7, 2026-06-14). The migration headers and `03-workspace/specs/2026-06-14-wms-bodyb-phase1-handoff.md` are the authoritative Body B record until one is written. Open WMS follow-ups: `F-Wave12-SUPPLY-PLAN-FULFILL-CONSUME-01` (per-consume automatic draw-down) and FEFO consumption (a later phase).

## 2026-06-14 SPA index budget lean-up SHIPPED (WMS B0 prerequisite cleared)

The SPA index budget lean-up (`F-Wave12-INDEX-BUDGET-HEADROOM-01`) is built and verified on branch `claude/index-leanup-sidebar-lazy` (not merged; no merge without the operator). The SPA index chunk drops from 39.99 to 33.7 kB gz under the held 40 kB `size-limit` budget. That is about 6 kB of reclaimed headroom, past the plan's at-or-under-37 target, so WMS B0 and the next several phases can add eager navigation weight without raising the budget.

The cut. One file. The left-nav Sidebar is lazy-split out of the always-on app shell (`apps/web/src/components/shell/AppShell.tsx`), so the sidebar mode config (`sidebarModes.ts`) and roughly fifty lucide-react navigation icons move into a `Sidebar-*.js` chunk instead of riding in the eager index. AppShell renders a fixed `w-56` rail placeholder behind a local `Suspense` boundary, so first paint shows no horizontal layout shift and the page-level Suspense never blanks. The chunk still loads on the first authenticated render, so the nav is present by the time the operator interacts.

Analysis first, per the plan. Measured with `npx vite-bundle-visualizer` (one-shot, no dependency added). The lucide icon set was the single largest eager contributor to the index (about 17.7 kB across 56 icon files); `routes.ts` was second (6.8 kB), left for the structural `F-Wave10-INDEX-SPLIT` lever. The sidebar carried the bulk of the eager icons, so lazy-loading it was the highest-leverage, lowest-risk single cut.

Gates green. typecheck, lint (max-warnings 0), contract parity 27, src unit 763, regression 519 passed plus 2 skipped (the `sidebarModes` exact-paths test 43 and `canon-steward` 3 both unaffected; sidebar structure did not change, only its load boundary), build, and size-limit. No edge, migration, money, RLS, audit, or idempotency change, so `deno check` is out of scope. An independent typescript-reviewer pass returned APPROVE with no critical or high findings; the one nit (fallback class divergence) was folded in.

Budget held at 40 kB, not raised, per the operator decision 2026-06-14. The raise stays reserved for a deliberate UI and navigation investment later.

Next. WMS Body B is on deck. The B0-to-B4 handoff is `03-workspace/specs/2026-06-14-wms-bodyb-phase1-handoff.md`. B0 (the `plugins.wms` chassis) is now unblocked. Before B1, lock the five B-decisions (location code scheme, putaway source linkage, lot capture point, `bin_stock_levels` grain, putaway done-movement no-op); the handoff recommends each. The B2 `stock_movements` `location_id` change remains the operator stop-point and ships in one PR with the sum-reconcile proof.

## 2026-06-13 3PL Supply Plan DB layer (Phase A5, backend) in PR #257

The Supply Plan DB layer is stacked on the Phase A4 work in PR #257 (not yet merged; no merge without the operator). It activates the dormant spine reservation path and adds the supply_plans engine. Kept on the A4 branch so migrations 0094 to 0097 stay contiguous. The A5 app layer (caps, three-pl-api routes, byte-mirror types, SPA) is handed off as the next slice.

Key finding: stock_levels.quantity_reserved (with quantity_available GENERATED as on_hand minus reserved) shipped in 0030 but was dormant. recompute_stock_level only derived on_hand and there was no reserve movement type. Migration 0095 activates it (adds reserve and reserve_release movement types, teaches recompute to derive reserved). Purely additive: the on_hand derivation is byte-identical and no reserve rows exist, so no current stock reading moves.

Tables: migration 0096 adds supply_plans (Pattern A, FSM draft / released / fulfilled / cancelled, warehouse_id, project_id) and supply_plan_lines (per item: required / available / reserved / shortage, resolution in reserve / inbound / purchase / replenish, nullable PO and receiving links). release_supply_plan reserves min(required, available) for reserve-resolution lines by writing 0095 reserve movements and records the shortage; cancel_supply_plan writes reserve_release to restore the spine reserved. Both are 3-arg cross-tenant-guarded SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (NOT_FOUND, never 403). Migration 0097 wires SUP- numbering. The audit_log entity_type CHECK is extended (supply_plan, supply_plan_line).

Validated on staging in aborting transactions: reserve then reserve_release moved quantity_reserved and the generated available correctly (10 to 6 to 10, on_hand steady at 10); a plan with a covered line (reserved 4, shortage 0) and a short line (reserved 10, shortage 5) released, the spine reserved tracking it, then cancelled back to zero.

Verified: SPA typecheck, lint (max-warnings 0), 759 unit plus 475 regression tests (including three new migration suites and the db-0083 authoritative-redefinition pin moved forward to 0096), contract parity. No SPA, edge, or type changes this slice, so build, size-limit, and deno check are unaffected from the A4 run.

Next: the A5 app layer (caps + three-pl-api supply_plan CRUD + release / cancel + byte-mirror types + SPA), handed off in `03-workspace/specs/2026-06-13-3pl-a5-supply-plan-dblayer-closeout-and-applayer-handoff.md`. Then A6 Job Runs.

## 2026-06-13 3PL project conversion with template snapshotting (Phase A4) in PR #257

Phase A4 of the 3PL commercial layer is up for review in PR #257 (not yet merged; no merge without the operator). It records which Job Builder template built a quote and the project it converts to, and freezes that template onto the project at conversion so later template edits never rewrite a project's origin.

Server: migration 0094 adds nullable `quotes.source_job_template_id` and `projects.source_job_template_id` (spine to 3PL add-on FK to `job_templates`, ON DELETE SET NULL) plus a nullable `projects.job_template_snapshot` jsonb. A forward redefinition of `convert_quote_to_project` (last in 0093, same 4-arg signature) copies the breadcrumb onto the project and builds the org-scoped frozen snapshot (header plus lines), reading both ids from the in-org quote row so the SECURITY DEFINER RPC cannot inject a foreign template. `quotes-api` validates `source_job_template_id` in-org via `assertRefInOrg` (404 not 403) on create and update. No new capability (rides `quotes.quote.write` and `quotes.convert_to_project`). Validated on staging in an aborting transaction (project carried the breadcrumb and a three-line snapshot).

SPA: the apply-template flow now stamps `source_job_template_id` on the quote alongside the job type, so the breadcrumb threads quote to project. The project detail page shows a "Built from template" link and a read-only TEMPLATE SNAPSHOT panel rendering the frozen lines. `source_job_template_id` and `job_template_snapshot` (plus `JobTemplateSnapshotSchema`) added to both byte-mirror `sales.ts` files.

Verified: contract parity (byte-mirror intact), SPA typecheck, lint (max-warnings 0), 456 tests (16 new: 11 migration static checks, 5 schema parse), deno check across all 29 edge bundles, build, size-limit (SPA index 39.58 kB gzipped, under 40).

Next: A5 Supply Plan. Handoff in `03-workspace/specs/2026-06-13-3pl-a4-template-snapshot-closeout-and-a5-handoff.md`. Stack onto the same branch; do not merge until the operator reviews.

## 2026-06-13 3PL Quote integration (Phase A3) in PR #256

Phase A3 of the 3PL commercial layer is up for review in PR #256 (not yet merged; no merge without the operator). Two pieces, matching the operator's two decisions (full A3 scope, SPA-thin expansion): a Job Builder template can be applied to a draft quote to expand its lines, and a quote now carries a job type that `convert_quote_to_project` copies onto the project so a won quote becomes a project of the right type.

Server: migration 0093 adds an additive nullable `quotes.job_type_id` (spine to spine FK to `job_types`, ON DELETE SET NULL) and forward-redefines `convert_quote_to_project` (last defined in 0044) to copy the job type onto the project. The RPC keeps its 4-arg signature and reads the value from the in-org quote row, so the SECURITY DEFINER function cannot inject a foreign job type; the cross-tenant guard and the line-item carryover are preserved. `projects.job_type_id` already exists (0016), so no project-side DDL. `quotes-api` create and update validate `job_type_id` in-org via `assertRefInOrg` (404, never 403); no new capability. `job_type_id` added to `QuoteSchema` and `CreateQuoteRequestSchema` in both byte-mirror `sales.ts` files.

SPA: a pure, unit-tested mapper (`lib/quotes/applyJobTemplate.ts`) turns template lines into quote line-add requests (component to item, service to vas, step to a priced free-text line when it has a rate or a note when it does not; `rate_cents` to `unit_price_cents`; `quantity` to `quantity_e3` via `Math.round`); priced labor steps carry their rate onto the quote total. `useApplyTemplateToQuote` sets the quote job type from the template then adds each line over the existing endpoint (not atomic by design; partial failure reports how many lines landed and the draft stays editable). `ApplyTemplatePanel` plus an inline job-type control on the quote detail page, both gated to editable states.

Verified: contract parity, SPA typecheck, lint (max-warnings 0), 440 tests plus 8 new mapper tests, deno check across all 25 bundles, build, size-limit (SPA index 39.46 kB gzipped, under 40). Migration validated on staging in a rollback transaction. Deferred to A4 by design: template snapshotting onto the project and the `source_job_template_id` breadcrumb. Closeout and A4 handoff: `03-workspace/specs/2026-06-13-3pl-a3-quote-integration-closeout-and-a4-handoff.md`. Follow-up F-Wave12-QUOTE-UPDATE-IMMUTABLE-FIELDS-01 (tighten the quote PATCH schema to omit immutable fields).

## 2026-06-04 3PL commercial pivot and WMS add-on (planning landed, execution started)

Moved the parked 3PL Job Builder pivot and the new WMS (warehouse execution) add-on from parked to planned, and started execution. The consolidated plan is `03-workspace/specs/2026-06-04-3pl-commercial-pivot-and-wms-pillar-plan.md`. Direction approved by the operator 2026-06-04.

Shape. 3PL Operations pivots from being thought of as the warehouse engine to being the commercial and operational planning layer (Accounts, Job Builders, Job Runs, Supply Plans, Billing Review, Job Profitability), keeping its light execution surfaces (receiving, shipments) under the existing gated `/3pl-operations/*`. WMS is a new sixth add-on, gated `plugins.wms` at a new `/wms/*` root, that deepens the spine's warehouse-level stock to bin level and never replaces it (a nullable `location_id` dimension on the existing `stock_movements` ledger; sum of bins equals the warehouse `quantity_on_hand`; turn it off and the totals are untouched). The five pillars are reframed as add-ons on the spine, matching the white paper V2 and the shipped spine reroute.

Decisions resolved 2026-06-04: spine plus add-ons framing with WMS as add-on six; 3PL commercial layer first, then the WMS deepening core; pillar-grouped sidebar (supersedes the UX-Q1 job-mode decision); name the service-relationship surface Accounts; reserve stock at project release and Supply Plan; manual Job Run scheduling first; simple Job-Run labor logging first.

Progress on branch `feat/spine-addons-canon-wms-adr` (PR #249, not merged): Phase A0 (canon: ADR 0002 plus the CLAUDE.md and 00-canon reframe) plus the Phase A1 Accounts backend, all green. The A1 backend is migrations 0089 (three_pl_accounts and account_service_definitions) and 0090 (ACC- numbering), both staging-validated in a rollback transaction; the types/threepl byte-mirror pair; the three-pl-api edge bundle; and the threepl.account.* capabilities. Next: the Phase A1 UI layer (the SPA Accounts pages plus the pillar-grouped sidebar), handed off to a fresh session in `03-workspace/specs/2026-06-04-3pl-accounts-ui-layer-handoff.md`. Stack onto the same branch; do not merge until the operator reviews.

## 2026-06-04 Spine plus add-ons SPA re-route (Phase 1)

Re-routed the SPA to the white-paper V2 "spine plus add-ons" IA. Spine and shared-building-block surfaces moved out of the plugin-gated `/3pl-operations/*` namespace to ungated neutral roots, so quoting, projects, vendors/POs/bills/expenses, catalog (items/BOMs/VAS), inventory (warehouses/stock), and sales-config are no longer gated by `plugins.three_pl`. Only the true 3PL add-on surfaces (receiving, shipments, and the production redirects) stay under `/3pl-operations/*`. Eight green commits on `claude/vigorous-stonebraker-24d5df`: redirect scaffolding (`RouteSpec.isRedirect` plus the generic `SpineMoveRedirect` that preserves params, query, and hash, plus a reframed `routes.test.ts`), then one commit per namespace (`/inventory`, `/catalog`, `/settings/sales-config`, `/purchasing`, `/quotes`, `/projects`, `/invoicing` creates). `inferPluginForPath` now gates only true add-on namespaces; every moved path keeps a `SpineMoveRedirect` entry so deep links survive. Every commit stayed green on typecheck, lint (max-warnings 0), 438 unit and regression tests, canon-steward, build, and size-limit. Front-end only: no edge, migration, money, audit, or idempotency changes. Page files stayed in place (lazy imports still point at `pages/3pl-operations/*`).

Open follow-ups:
- **`F-Wave10-SPINE-EDGE-GATE-RECONCILE-01`**: the edge bundles quotes-api, projects-api, and inventory-api still hard-gate `plugins.three_pl` while their SPA surfaces are now ungated spine. Harmless today (three_pl defaults on for every tier, so the gate always passes) but the edge should widen to an anyOf predicate or ungate so the spine is truly always-on server-side.
- **`F-Wave10-SEARCH-API-REROUTE-HREF-01`**: search-api emits `/3pl-operations/quotes/:id` and `/3pl-operations/projects/:id` result hrefs (edge). Deep-link redirects catch the clicks today; `search-api-href-routes.test.ts` locks the old prefix until this lands.
- **`F-Wave10-SPINE-REROUTE-REDIRECT-RETIRE-01`**: drop the `SpineMoveRedirect` entries and their canon-steward allowlist rows once analytics confirm no live bookmarks land on the old `/3pl-operations/*` spine paths.
- **`F-Wave10-SPINE-PAGE-DIR-RELOCATE-01`** (optional): relocate the moved page directories from `pages/3pl-operations/*` to mirror their new URLs.
- **`F-Wave10-LEGACY-PRODUCTION-REDIRECT-MIGRATE-01`** (optional): fold the two `LegacyProductionRedirect` components into the generic `SpineMoveRedirect`.

Plan and full detail: `03-workspace/plans/2026-06-04-spine-plus-addons-reroute.md`.

Last updated: 2026-06-04 (Cross-tenant foreign-key security gap CLOSED end to end, plus an edge-function Deno typecheck gate and the FK-validation follow-ups, across four PRs merged to prod (#238, #240, #241, #242) and one closed as superseded (#239). The session opened with a 73-agent read-only optimization audit (report untracked in audit-output/, grade B plus, constitution holding: 21 byte-mirror pairs identical, RLS Pattern A explicit org_id binding across handlers, money and idempotency and plugin gates compliant), which confirmed the cross-tenant FK class as the top risk. Root cause: every foreign key in the schema is a plain single-column constraint that checks existence not org (zero composite id-plus-org_id FKs), so a service-role insert or update could persist a client-supplied FK pointing at another tenant's row; the proven breach was payment apply and credit-note apply taking an invoice_id validated only as a UUID, after which the recompute triggers mutated the victim org's invoice and forged an audit_log row. PR #238 adds a shared assertRefInOrg helper (org-scoped existence check, returns 404 NOT_FOUND never 403) called before every client-supplied FK write across 14 bundles and about 129 call sites; the polymorphic activities.entity_id fails closed on an unmapped type, owner_user_id validates org_memberships.user_id, quote_line_items is skipped (no org_id, parent-scoped via its quote). Coverage was verified against the authoritative pg_constraint list, which caught gaps the scoping agents missed (shifts team_id and warehouse_id, copack fulfillment warehouse_id and shipment_id, quotes default_tax_id plus payment_method_id plus pricing_tier_id, projects job_type_id, the imports raw-row FK columns). The new validation broke three regression mocks that did not seed the parent rows; CI caught it pre-merge and the fix seeds warehouses and projects in those state builders, plus a Category 12 cross-tenant 404 probe block in rls-probe.spec.ts (payment apply, credit-note apply, and PO create with a foreign tenant id all 404). PR #241 makes the edge functions Deno-clean (47 pre-existing type errors that esbuild transpile never caught: 44 the untyped service-role client cast pattern resolved with an as unknown as cast, a dashboard-api helper mistyped as PostgrestQueryBuilder versus PostgrestFilterBuilder that cascaded into eight property-access errors, and a leads converted-status backstop preserved via a cast) and enables a deno check CI gate over every bundle entry point, so future PRs typecheck the edge functions instead of only catching errors post-merge at deploy. PR #240 fixed the two substantive type errors the gate surfaced: the stripe-webhook apiVersion pin cast to Stripe.LatestApiVersion (the deliberate 2024-09-30.acacia pin kept, zero runtime change) and the kitforce clock-in rate coerced from the integer-or-string money wire type before the comparison. PR #242 closed the three FK-validation follow-ups: assertRefInOrg now filters soft-deleted parents by default (the 3 parents with no deleted_at column, chart_of_accounts and expense_categories and org_memberships, opt out with softDelete false), a new assertRefsInOrg batches the journal-entry-line and imports FK checks into one IN query, and the imports commit inserts the Zod-parsed row plus server-set org_id and created_by and updated_by instead of the raw client row, closing MASSG-IMPORTS-01 so a client can no longer inject created_by or id or status or any undeclared column. New finding filed separately: the import RowSchemas declare wrong column names (invoice number vs invoice_number, customer email and phone vs primary_email and primary_phone, item unit_of_measure vs unit_id, expense number vs expense_number), so the import feature is likely broken for four of five entities; #242 did not touch the import wire contract, only the insert allowlist. Verified throughout with a locally installed Deno 2.1.4 (deno check exit 0 on all 28 bundles) and pnpm filter web test (724 src plus 438 regression green); all four merges deployed via deploy-functions with the FK fix live in prod, and the Deno gate validated #242 on the PR itself. Constitutional invariants held: 404 not 403 on cross-tenant writes, no byte-mirror touched, forward-only with no migration in any PR, RLS and money and idempotency and audit_log observed only, no new dependency, brand voice on disk. Process notes: drive FK coverage from pg_constraint not agent enumeration; always branch from current origin/main when prior session PRs have merged (a stale-main branch needed a rebase); one reviewer agent false-flagged credit_notes as bundling a security change into the Deno cleanup, but the real diff was two casts (already-merged content mis-attributed as new). Open: the import column-mapping fix, plus lower-priority audit polish (DataTable column sort F-Wave10-UI-KIT-DATATABLE-SORT-01, server pagination F-WS7-SERVER-PAGINATION, index-coverage migrations, auth-api getUserById N+1 batching) and the audit's 16 residual high-density sub-areas in audit-output/raw-findings.json under stillHigh. Closeout journal at 03-workspace/journal/2026-06-04-fk-security-deno-gate-closeout.md. Recorded in memory fk_cross_tenant_fix_pr238.md and read_only_optimization_audit_2026_06_03.md.)

- `F-Wave9-FONT-DECODE-ERROR-01`: production console emitted `Failed to decode downloaded font` and `OTS parsing error: invalid sfntVersion: 1008821359` on every page load. Root cause was NOT the Google Fonts CDN URL (all three families resolved 200 with valid CSS); the real culprit was four unresolved `@font-face` declarations in `apps/web/src/styles.css` pointing at `/fonts/BebasNeue-Regular.woff2`, `/fonts/InterTight-Regular.woff2`, `/fonts/InterTight-Medium.woff2`, and `/fonts/JetBrainsMono-Regular.woff2`. The Wave 1 `F-Wave1-FONTS-01` follow-up to drop self-hosted woff2 files into `apps/web/public/fonts/` never landed (per `apps/web/public/fonts/README.txt`), so Chrome requested those paths, got the SPA shell HTML back via the catch-all rewrite, and OTS rejected the `<!doctype html>` magic bytes (`0x3C21646F` decoded as `<!do` matches the reported invalid sfntVersion `1008821359`). Fix removes the four broken `@font-face` blocks; the Google Fonts `<link>` in `apps/web/index.html` (preconnected to `fonts.googleapis.com` and `fonts.gstatic.com`) already provides all three families with the right weights, so the CSS family declarations in styles.css resolve cleanly via the CDN. `F-Wave1-FONTS-01` (self-hosted woff2 swap) remains open as the long-term target. Build green at 30.03 kB / 40 kB main chunk.
- `F-Wave8-NIGHTLY-RLS-PROBE-INVESTIGATE-01`: root cause was that there is no staging deploy workflow. `.github/workflows/deploy-functions.yml` shipped a single `deploy` job pinned to `environment: production-functions` and `secrets.SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF` (prod project), so every PR's handler changes reached prod but never the Supabase staging branch. The 8 failing probe rows in run `26160350927` were PR #48's new `?customer_id=` / `?vendor_id=` / `?project_id=` filter probes hitting staging handlers that predated the LISTFILTER-01 ship. Fix shape: a second job `deploy_staging` added to the SAME workflow file, mirroring prod exactly except for `environment: staging`, the `--project-ref` arg sourcing `secrets.STAGING_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF`, and `needs: deploy` so prod ships first (defensive ordering; staging is the downstream verifier). To prevent drift, the `BUNDLES` list moved from a per-job shell array to a single workflow-level `env.BUNDLES` multi-line string consumed by both jobs via `while IFS= read -r bundle`. The repo-level `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` is owner-scoped and works against any project the owner owns, so the same secret deploys both targets (no new access-token provisioning). Operator action required before the workflow first fires: add `STAGING_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF = dnkgaufydcnedgkuoyml` to the `staging` GH Actions environment. After that, the next nightly-rls-probe run goes green.
- `F-Wave5-CO-01-EDGE-01`: Deno-side Sentry capture wired into the Edge Function bundle via the central `route()` dispatcher in `supabase/functions/_shared/route.ts`. SDK choice: **HTTP-transport** (not `@sentry/deno`). Rationale: zero new top-level dependencies, zero per-function bundle delta sprawl across 21 functions, full control over the PII scrub posture, and side-steps the unverified `@sentry/deno`-on-Supabase-Edge-runtime risk. The new module at `supabase/functions/_shared/sentry.ts` synthesises a Sentry envelope (per https://develop.sentry.dev/sdk/envelopes/) and POSTs to `<dsn>.ingest.sentry.io/api/<projectId>/envelope/` with the runtime's built-in `fetch`. PII contract is byte-identical in posture to the SPA wrapper: `event.user.email` / `username` stripped, `event.user.ip_address` pinned to `null` (the Relay opt-out signal · not `delete`, per PR #67), `event.request.cookies` deleted, `event.request.headers.authorization` and `Authorization` (both cases) deleted, `event.request.url` canonicalised to `origin + pathname`, `event.request.query_string` deleted, email and phone regex redactions on `event.extra` and `event.tags`, and the belt-and-suspenders drop when the message or any exception value still matches an email pattern after the per-field scrub. The `route()` catch arm captures only the INTERNAL_ERROR class (non-`ApiError`); `ApiError` 4xx are intentionally NOT captured to keep Sentry signal-to-noise clean. Context shape: `{ route: <matched pattern>, method, bundle, request_id, url: origin+pathname, org_id (opaque Supabase UUID only when present) }`. Cold-start `initSentry()` is idempotent and a no-op when `SENTRY_DSN` is absent. Tests at `apps/web/test/regression/edge-sentry.test.ts` (19 assertions; same chassis as the existing Deno-targeted regression suites via `vitest.regression.config.ts`). Env documented in new `supabase/functions/.env.example` with the SERVER-SIDE-ONLY warning intact. **Operator action required:** create a separate Sentry **Deno** project at https://sentry.io (recommended: distinct from the existing SPA project so JavaScript-React and edge-server error classes stay visually separated; the operator may merge into one project later by pointing the same DSN at both), copy the new project's server-side DSN, and set `supabase secrets set SENTRY_DSN=<dsn>` (or in the Supabase dashboard under Edge Function Secrets). The Edge DSN must NEVER be the SPA's `VITE_SENTRY_DSN`. Journal at `03-workspace/journal/phase-9-sentry-edge.md`. Constitutional invariants: zero new top-level deps, no schema / migration / RLS / audit_log / idempotency / capability surface change.

- `F-Wave5-CO-01` / `F-Wave3-OBS-01` (SPA portion, partial close): Sentry SaaS error + performance capture wired into the SPA. New `apps/web/src/lib/sentry.ts` is a typed wrapper around `@sentry/react@^8.40.0` (MIT, operator approved as a new top-level dep) modelled directly on the F-Wave5-CO-02 PostHog wrapper: lazy-loaded via dynamic `import('@sentry/react')` inside `initSentry`, named `manualChunks.sentry` in `vite.config.ts`, no-op when `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` is absent at build (tree-shakes to zero chunk emission and ~0.09 kB main-bundle delta). `main.tsx` fires `void initSentry()` BEFORE `ReactDOM.createRoot(...).render(...)` so render-time errors during the very first paint are captured; `ErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch` forwards `error` plus `info.componentStack` via `captureException`; `AuthContext.signIn` / cold-mount recovery call `identifySentryUser(user.id)` with the opaque Supabase UUID (never email or PII), `AuthContext.signOut` calls `resetSentryUser()` so post-sign-out crashes are not attributed to the previous user. **PII posture** (constitutional, asserted by unit tests): `beforeSend` scrub strips `event.user.email` / `user.username` / `user.ip_address` (keeps only `id`), `event.request.cookies`, `event.request.headers.authorization` (both cases), URL query strings, and redacts email / phone regex matches in `event.extra` and `event.tags` to `[redacted]`; events whose message or exception value contains an email pattern after the per-field scrub are dropped entirely; `sendDefaultPii: false` at init refuses IP and cookies by default. **Sample rates** (operator-overridable via env without redeploy): `tracesSampleRate: 0.1` (conservative 10 percent), `replaysSessionSampleRate: 0.0` (no baseline session record), `replaysOnErrorSampleRate: 1.0` (always capture replay when an error fires). **Replay masking**: `maskAllInputs: true`, `blockAllMedia: true` (matches the PostHog session-recording posture). **Bundle posture**: main `index-*.js` chunk lands at **29.95 kB / 40 kB** gzipped (was 29.94 kB; +0.09 kB delta from the wrapper, well under threshold). With `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` set at build, a separate `sentry-<hash>.js` chunk emits; with the DSN unset, the entire `@sentry/react` import is tree-shaken (no chunk, no bytes). New unit test at `apps/web/src/lib/sentry.test.ts` covers 15 assertions: init no-op without DSN, init idempotency, identify / reset / capture short-circuit when uninitialised, and 9 PII-scrub assertions including email / phone redaction, Authorization header strip (both cases), cookie strip, query-string strip, user-id retention, message-pattern drop, exception-value drop, benign event passthrough. Env vars documented in `apps/web/.env.example` and typed in `apps/web/src/vite-env.d.ts`: `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` (required to activate; absent = no-op), `VITE_SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` (defaults to `VITE_APP_ENV`), `VITE_SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE` (defaults to `0.1`), `VITE_SENTRY_REPLAY_SESSION_SAMPLE_RATE` (defaults to `0.0`). Operator next steps to activate: 1) create a Sentry org + React/Browser project at sentry.io, 2) copy the public DSN from Client Keys (frontend-safe by design, rate-limited per project), 3) set `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` in Vercel env vars for Production + Preview (leave Development unset so local `pnpm dev` stays in no-op posture), 4) redeploy, 5) trigger a synthetic error and verify capture arrives in Sentry within 30 seconds with no PII in payload. Edge-function (Deno-side) Sentry capture is OUT OF SCOPE for this PR and filed as `F-Wave5-CO-01-EDGE-01`; source-map upload is filed as `F-Wave9-SENTRY-SOURCEMAPS-01`. Journal at `03-workspace/journal/phase-9-sentry-spa.md`.
- `F-Wave5-CO-01` / `F-Wave3-OBS-01` SPA activation + Relay-IP hardening (2026-05-20): operator activated Sentry SaaS at sentry.io, project `4511423235751936` on US region, DSN set in Vercel via GitHub repo secrets per PR #66 (`3e4fba6`). Sentry Issue `JAVASCRIPT-REACT-1` captured via a controlled click-throw smoke test from incognito Chrome, event ID `64a6acc3`. Initial event surfaced a constitutional PII gate breach: source IP `98.172.8.242` and city-level geography `Fayetteville, US` appeared in the event despite `sendDefaultPii: false` plus `beforeSend` IP delete. Root cause: Sentry's server-side Relay enriches events with IP from the request source unless `ip_address` arrives as `null` (treated as opt-out) AND the project-level Security & Privacy → "Prevent Storing of IP Addresses" toggle is ON. Two-part fix shipped in this PR: 1) operator flipped the project toggle (60-second action); 2) `apps/web/src/lib/sentry.ts` `beforeSend` now sets `event.user.ip_address = null` explicitly rather than `delete`, and synthesises a `{ ip_address: null }` user object even when the input had none, so anonymous events still carry the opt-out signal. Three new unit-test assertions in `apps/web/src/lib/sentry.test.ts` cover the contract: with user.id, without user.id (only PII fields present), and no user object at all (all 16 tests passing). The original chassis claim that "`sendDefaultPii: false` refuses IP and cookies by default" was technically true at the SDK layer but incomplete; corrected in the journal's new "Activation" section. Bundle posture unchanged at 29.95 kB / 40 kB. Three new follow-ups filed during the close: `F-Wave9-NODE20-DEPRECATION-01` (GitHub Actions Node.js 20 deprecation by June 2026), `F-Wave9-VERCEL-NATIVE-BUILD-CONSIDER-01` (whether to migrate deploy off GitHub Actions to render the Sensitive-flag gotcha class architecturally moot), `F-Wave9-FONT-DECODE-ERROR-01` (production console font-decode errors surfaced during the verification dive). - `F-Wave9-SENTRY-SOURCEMAPS-01`: production source-map upload via `@sentry/vite-plugin@^5.3.0` (MIT). The plugin runs at the end of the Vite build, uploads emitted `.map` files to Sentry (so Sentry deminifies stack traces server-side), and then deletes the maps from `dist/` via `sourcemaps.filesToDeleteAfterUpload`. Build posture: `build.sourcemap: 'hidden'` emits maps to `dist/` but strips the `//# sourceMappingURL=` comment from JS chunks, so the SPA never advertises map location to a browser (private maps, per operator decision). The plugin is added as a **devDependency** in `apps/web/package.json` only; the top-level `package.json` is untouched and the SPA bundle delta is zero (plugin runs at build time only, ships nothing). When `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is absent at build the plugin no-ops via the `disable` flag and the build still ships a working bundle (maps stay un-uploaded, errors arrive at Sentry with minified frames). When the token IS set, the plugin reads `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, and a `release.name` derived from `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` (Vercel injects this at build time; falls back to `local-dev` for local builds). Crucially, none of the three env vars carries a `VITE_` prefix so Vite's `define` step never substitutes them into the SPA bundle. **Contract test** at `apps/web/test/regression/sentry-auth-leak.test.ts` enforces this against future regressions: after every production build, it scans every file under `dist/` and fails if any chunk contains the literal substring `sentry_auth` (case-insensitive); also asserts no chunk contains the literal `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` value when one is set at test runtime. Synthetic-leak verified during PR development by appending `sentry_auth=fake_token_for_test` to a chunk; the test failed as expected; chunk restored before commit. **Workflow integration**: `.github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml` now injects all three secrets at the `vercel build` step's `env:` block via GitHub repo secrets, mirroring the established pattern for `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY` and `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` from PR #66. **Operator action required** to activate: 1) provision `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` at Sentry → Settings → Auth Tokens (scope: `project:releases` only, no other scopes needed; do NOT mix with org-level tokens), 2) set `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` in BOTH Vercel Environment Variables (Production + Preview scopes) AND GitHub repo Secrets (the GitHub copy is what the workflow reads; the Vercel copy is for fallback should the workflow architecture ever migrate to Vercel-native build). 3) Verify: trigger a Vercel redeploy, capture a real production error via Sentry → Issues, confirm the stack frames show readable file names and line numbers (e.g. `apps/web/src/pages/.../FooPage.tsx:42:7`) instead of minified shapes like `index-Xyz.js:1:18234`. **Rotation cadence**: annual. Operator should rotate `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` once per year and update both the Vercel env var and the GitHub repo secret in the same operator session. Bundle posture unchanged at 29.92 kB / 40 kB; the plugin import adds ~0.04 kB to the main chunk via the Vite config (well under the 0.5 kB threshold). Journal: appended "Source maps wired" section to `03-workspace/journal/phase-9-sentry-spa.md`.
- `F-Wave8-PDF-FONT-EMBED-01` + `F-Wave8-PDF-QUOTE-DOWNLOAD-01` + `F-Wave8-PDF-PO-DOWNLOAD-01`: PDF polish bundle landed as one PR. **Font embedding:** Bebas Neue (display, 56 KB) and Inter Tight (body, 298 KB) ship under SIL Open Font License 1.1 and are committed under `supabase/functions/pdf-worker/fonts/` alongside `LICENSE.txt`. `scripts/encode-fonts.mjs` (Node 20+, zero deps) emits a generated `supabase/functions/pdf-worker/fonts.ts` module that exports the two fonts as base64 string constants; the worker registers them via `doc.addFileToVFS` + `doc.addFont` and switches every `setFont('helvetica', ...)` call to `setFont('BebasNeue', 'normal')` (display text: KITSTAK wordmark, document-type label, section labels, TOTAL row) or `setFont('InterTight', 'normal')` (body text: customer / vendor name, line items, footer, subtotal / tax rows). No bold or italic weights embedded because neither free-tier font ships them at OFL terms; if a future template needs them, embed the matching .ttf and file a follow-up. **Worker bundle delta:** the worker pulls in ~354 KB of raw font bytes plus base64 overhead (~474 KB total `fonts.ts`); well under the 50 MB Edge Function deploy limit. **SPA bundle delta:** zero. ### Closed in this session

- `F-Wave8-POSTHOG-FEATURE-FLAGS-01`: PostHog feature flags layered on top of the existing server-side `useOrgFlags()` pattern. **Precedence rule (constitutional):** server-side flags via `useOrgFlags()` are AUTHORITATIVE. PostHog layers on top for gradual rollout and A/B-test experiments, but a server-side `false` always wins — PostHog can narrow a server-true to false (rollout cohort) or split server-true across variants (A/B), but NEVER flip a server-false to true. This protects the `403 FEATURE_DISABLED { flag }` contract: the server enforces actual access. Two new typed wrappers on `apps/web/src/lib/analytics.ts` (`getPostHogFlag`, `onPostHogFlagsLoaded`) thin-wrap `posthog.getFeatureFlag` and `posthog.onFeatureFlags` without taking a position on precedence. New pure `apps/web/src/lib/hooks/featureFlagResolver.ts` carries the precedence logic in a React-free module so the unit tests run without jsdom. New `apps/web/src/lib/hooks/useFeatureFlag(key)` hook composes `useOrgFlags()` plus the PostHog cache plus the resolver, with an `onFeatureFlags` subscription to drive re-renders when /decide returns mid-session. Return shape: `{ isEnabled: boolean; source: 'server' | 'posthog' | 'default'; variant: string | null; isLoading: boolean }`. **No existing call site migrated.** `useOrgFlags()` keeps its existing semantics; every current consumer (Sidebar pillar gates, `RequireFlag` route guards) continues to read server-only truth so route 403s stay PostHog-uninfluenced. The new hook is the surface for experiments and gradual rollouts that the feature team explicitly opts into; per-feature adoption is a separate decision. **Bundle posture:** no new dep (`posthog-js` already in the tree from F-Wave5-CO-02); main `index-*.js` lands at **29.98 kB / 40 kB** gzipped (was 29.92 after the source-maps merge; +0.06 kB delta from the two analytics wrappers and the resolver, well under threshold). **Tests:** 16 new assertions in `apps/web/src/lib/hooks/featureFlagResolver.test.ts`. Precedence matrix covered: server-true + posthog-{true,false,undefined}; server-false + posthog-{true,string,undefined}; server-absent (off) + posthog-true; server-loading; multivariate variant; empty-variant edge case. The critical row — `server-FALSE + posthog-TRUE => DISABLED, source: server` — is the constitutional gate. Analytics wrappers covered for both the not-initialised no-DSN posture and against a stubbed PostHog handle. All 37 SPA unit tests pass (16 new + 16 sentry + 5 money). Journal extension at `03-workspace/journal/phase-8-posthog-analytics.md` under "Feature flag layering" with the full precedence rule, hook usage example, and when-to-use-which guidance.

### Process-level: DRIFTS that surfaced + codified responses

1. **Wave 2's disjoint-domain dispatch produced 0 cross-domain seams.** Six agents each shipped a domain CRUD; nobody owned the seams between domains. 41 gaps surfaced when operator exercised quote-to-cash end-to-end. **Response**: Phase 6.5 codified Shape B (shared-UI agent + schema/RPC agent before dependent-UI agents) as the future-wave pattern. Documented in `wave-6-5-workflow-integration.md` lessons section.

2. **Canon Steward missed a TODO placeholder during consolidation.** Agent 6.5-A shipped `ProjectLineItemPlaceholder` in `useProjects.ts` with a TODO marker for the orchestrator to replace once 6.5-B's real `ProjectLineItem` type landed. The Canon Steward pass missed the marker. The placeholder field names (`quantity_e3`, `line_total_cents`) did not match the real schema (`quantity`, `discount_percent`, no precomputed total); `formatCents(undefined)` threw at first render of a real row, ErrorBoundary caught. Operator caught it at re-test. **Response**: hotfix PR #21 replaced the placeholder; `F-Wave7-CANON-STEWARD-01` codifies a pre-commit grep guardrail.

3. **String-literal drift across boundaries: recurring pattern.** Two instances in two consecutive waves: CORS allow-headers (`cors.ts` and `responses.ts` drifted; `F-Wave6-CORS-01`) and feature flag key (`ops-api` read `plugins.3pl` while `seed_org_settings` wrote `plugins.three_pl`; `G-OPS-FLAG-01`). Same class of bug. **Response**: both closed in this session (PR #18 + PR #19). `F-Wave7-LITDRIFT-01` spawns a sweep to canonicalize all cross-boundary string literals in `_shared/`.

4. **Transient API blips during agent runs.** Phase 6.5 Stage agents hit API connection errors mid-run three times (twice in Stage 1, once in Stage 2). Each agent had landed ~95% of deliverables before failing. **Response**: discovered the finisher-agent recovery pattern. Spawn a small follow-up agent with the residual scope (specific files to fix, specific gates to pass) as its charter. Faster than re-dispatching the full Stage agent and the partial work is durable. Documented in `wave-6-5-workflow-integration.md` and now codified in `SESSION-CATALYST.md`.

5. **48-probe matrix is necessary but not sufficient.** Probes hit edge functions directly with service-role JWTs; they cannot surface SPA-edge integration gaps or cross-domain workflow gaps. Phase 6 chassis revealed 4 such bugs (apiClient URL, CORS, Sidebar paths, Sidebar expansion); Phase 6.5 audit revealed 41 more. The only existing cross-domain verifier is the operator running `F-Wave6-FLOW-01` by hand. **Response**: tracked under `F-Wave5-TEST-02` (smoke selector hardening) but scope needs to grow into a real browser-driven workflow smoke that walks one full quote-to-cash chain pre-merge.

Four rapid-fire hotfixes landed all the foundational SPA -> edge-function wiring gaps that Wave 5's probe matrix could not have caught: apiClient relative URLs + missing auth headers (PR #13), CORS allow-headers missing `apikey` (PR #14), Sidebar pillar paths drifted from the routes table (PR #15), Sidebar surfaced only pillars while the Phase 6 quote-to-cash flow needs Workspace / Sales / Procurement / Inventory / Finance / Tools / Admin (PR #16). Plus an operator-data fixup seeding `org_feature_flags` for the `kitstak` org (which had been provisioned before migration 0040's `seed_org_settings` shipped). Phase 6 chassis closed; the operator-led quote-to-cash workflow exercise is the remaining Phase 6 gate.

**Wave 5 probes closed at 48 / 48 green on staging (PR #9 + PR #10 merged · commits `32d7acd` and `ebe8f5d`).** Phase 4 (marketing site) skipped at operator direction (built in parallel outside this session). Phase 5 shipped the 48-probe RLS matrix; the matrix's first real run surfaced six constitutional violations which the same phase resolved via four hotfixes: Node 22 in the probe workflow (native WebSocket), staging branch rebase to apply 37 Wave 2 migrations, probe seed schema corrections, and the substantive 403→404 fixes (quotes-api / projects-api side-car capability shims, admin-console-api `verify_jwt = false`, and forward migration `0041` redefining `convert_quote_to_project` to take `p_caller_org_id` explicitly). Final probe run: 48 / 48 in 31s. Sentry and analytics remain deferred per operator.

**Wave 3 integration shipped (PR #8 merged · commit `209c106`).** AuditTimeline mounted on every state-having detail page (13 total); Sidebar live `useOrgFlags()`; global `ErrorBoundary`; NotFoundPage dual-import Vite warning fixed; `apps/web/playwright.config.ts` plus smoke + rls-probe scaffolds.

### Wave 2 second hotfix (PR #6, merged · commit `1cfdcf6`)

PR #5's hotfix unblocked the pooler connection and CLI version. The next `deploy-functions` run advanced past those errors and deployed the first two bundles (`audit-chain-verify`, `idempotency-gc`), then failed on `auth-api` with `Relative import path "zod" not prefixed with / or ./ or ../`. The Supabase Preview check on the same SHA failed the same way. Root cause: all 6 side-car type files use bare `from 'zod'`, which the SPA resolves via `node_modules` but Deno cannot resolve without an import map. Fix: `supabase/functions/deno.json` ships a workspace import map (`"zod": "npm:zod@3.23.8"`) and the deploy workflow passes `--import-map` explicitly. No canon files touched; byte-mirror parity intact (`test:contract` 25 / 25).

After this hotfix merged, all 3 post-merge workflows turned green (`ci`, `deploy-functions`, `deploy-prod`). All 23 edge function bundles deployed successfully per the deploy log.

### Wave 2 first hotfix (PR #5, merged · commit `2057391`)

Two GitHub Actions failures after PR #4 merge required a hotfix:

- `migrate.yml` used `aws-1-us-west-2.pooler.supabase.com`; the project's region is `us-west-1` and the canonical pooler hostname is `aws-0-us-west-1.pooler.supabase.com`. ENOTFOUND on the DNS lookup.
- `deploy-functions.yml` pinned the Supabase CLI at `1.180.0`, which predates Postgres 17 GA support and rejects `db.major_version = 17` in `config.toml`. The remote project IS on Postgres 17.x, so the correct fix is bumping the CLI, not lowering the config.

Both workflows now pin `supabase/setup-cli@v1` with `version: latest`. `deploy-functions.yml` BUNDLES array extended to all 23 functions (Wave 1's 2 plus Wave 2's 21). `config.toml` adds `[functions.tenants-api] verify_jwt = false` so the public host-resolver route serves pre-auth (closes `F-Wave2-AGENT-A-06`).

## Phase 5 close (hotfixes that landed during the phase)

The probe matrix's first real run surfaced six constitutional violations the matrix was designed to catch. All resolved in the same phase, on top of three infrastructure hotfixes to unblock the probe runtime:

1. **Probe workflow on Node 22** (`9a0eaf8`). `@supabase/realtime-js@2.105+` requires native WebSocket; Node 20 lacks it. Bumped just `nightly-rls-probe.yml`'s `actions/setup-node` to Node 22. Other workflows stay on Node 20.
2. **Staging branch rebase** (no code change). The Supabase preview branch `staging` was created at migration 0003 and missed all 37 Wave 2 migrations. Rebased via the Supabase Management API; the rebase also redeploys functions from main onto staging.
3. **Probe seed schema corrections** (`fe913e6`). The probe's fixture bootstrap used several wrong column names (`name` → `display_name` on warehouses; `given_name` / `family_name` → `first_name` / `last_name` on contacts; `state` → `status` on leads / invoices / credit notes / purchase_orders / vendor_bills / expenses / journal_entries; `title` → `display_name` and `state` → `stage` on opportunities; `posted_on` → `entry_date` on journal_entries); missing required document numbers and period_year / period_month on journal entries; `amount_cents 0` on payments (CHECK > 0).
4. **Constitutional 403→404 / 401→404 fixes** (`ae02e8c`). Two patterns:
   - Quotes-api and projects-api imported `requireCap` from the singular handler-helpers, which only knows the 14 `org.*` capabilities. Every `quotes.*` / `projects.*` cap check returned `FORBIDDEN`. Fix: per-bundle `_helpers.ts` with `requireSalesCap` wrapping the side-car `SALES_CAPABILITIES_BY_ROLE`, mirroring the invoicing-api pattern. The singular byte-mirrored `_shared/capabilities.ts` was not touched.
   - Admin-console-api had `verify_jwt = true` so the Supabase gateway returned 401 to anonymous callers before the handler could throw its 404. Fix: `[functions.admin-console-api] verify_jwt = false` in `config.toml` (handler already correctly returns 404 for anonymous).
5. **Forward migration `0041`** (`ebe8f5d`). The probe still saw 409 STATE_CONFLICT cross-tenant on `quotes-api convert-to-project`. Root cause: `convert_quote_to_project` checked `v_org_id <> public.current_org_id()`, but the handler invokes the RPC via the service-role client, which has no JWT claim. `current_org_id()` returned NULL; the comparison evaluated to NULL (treated as false); the cross-tenant guard never fired; the next check (`state != 'approved'`) won. Fix: drop the 3-arg RPC, recreate as 4-arg taking `p_caller_org_id`, surface mismatch as `NOT_FOUND`. Handler passes `caller.orgId`. Forward-only; idempotent.

**Final probe run on commit `ebe8f5d`**: 48 / 48 passed in 31s.

## Wave 6 remaining work (operator-led quote-to-cash exercise)

Phase 6 gate per `SESSION-CATALYST.md` §9: "operator successfully exercises the full Pillar-1 workflow on prod, every state-change writes audit_log, no 500s." The chassis is now wired. The exercise itself is the next step:

1. Sign in to `www.kitstak.com` as `mike@kitstak.com` against the seeded `kitstak` org.
2. **Workspace -> Customers -> New**: create a customer.
3. **Sales -> Quotes -> New** (against that customer) -> Send -> Accept -> Convert to Project.
4. **Sales -> Invoices -> New** (against that project) -> Send -> Post payment.
5. **3PL Operations -> Receiving** -> create one and complete.
6. **3PL Operations -> Shipments** -> create one and ship.
7. Every detail page should render an `AuditTimeline` section with rows.

Tracked as `F-Wave6-FLOW-01`. Any small gaps surfaced during the exercise (missing copy, missing buttons, capability-gate corrections, broken navigation) are fixed inline per the Phase 6 protocol.
